questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 8 km/h, while it takes 2 hours for the boat to cover a distance of 20 km downstream. What is the speed (in km/h) of the stream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The speed of a boat in still water = 8 km/h

Time taken to cover 20 km downstream = 2 hours

**Formula used:**

Speed downstream = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

Distance = Speed x Time

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed downstream = 20 km / 2 h

⇒ Speed downstream = 10 km/h

Speed downstream = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

⇒ 10 km/h = 8 km/h + Speed of stream

⇒ Speed of stream = 10 km/h - 8 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream = 2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A solution of phenyl and water is 28 litres, with phenyl and water in ratio 4 : 3. 21 litres phenyl-water solution which has phenyl to water ratio as 2 : 1 is added to the 28 litres phenyl-water solution. Again 51 litres phenyl-water solution that has phenyl to water ratio as 9 : 8 is added to this. What is ratio of water to phenyl in the final mixture?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A solution of phenyl and water is 28 litres, with phenyl and water in ratio 4 : 3.

21 litres phenyl-water solution which has phenyl to water ratio as 2 : 1 is added.

51 litres phenyl-water solution that has phenyl to water ratio as 9 : 8 is added.

**Formula used:**

Volume of phenyl = Total volume × (Phenyl ratio / (Phenyl ratio + Water ratio))

Volume of water = Total volume × (Water ratio / (Phenyl ratio + Water ratio))

**Calculation:**

Initial solution: 28 litres

Phenyl = 28 × (4 / (4 + 3)) = 28 × (4 / 7) = 16 litres

Water = 28 × (3 / (4 + 3)) = 28 × (3 / 7) = 12 litres

Second solution: 21 litres (Phenyl:Water = 2:1)

Phenyl = 21 × (2 / (2 + 1)) = 21 × (2 / 3) = 14 litres

Water = 21 × (1 / (2 + 1)) = 21 × (1 / 3) = 7 litres

Third solution: 51 litres (Phenyl:Water = 9:8)

Phenyl = 51 × (9 / (9 + 8)) = 51 × (9 / 17) = 27 litres

Water = 51 × (8 / (9 + 8)) = 51 × (8 / 17) = 24 litres

Total phenyl = 16 + 14 + 27 = 57 litres

Total water = 12 + 7 + 24 = 43 litres

⇒ Ratio of water to phenyl = 43 : 57

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A specific amount of money is loaned out at a simple interest rate, resulting in ₹15,000 in 2 years and ₹20,000 in 4 years. The rate percentage per annum is:
questions.solution:

A specific amount of money results in ₹15,000 in 2 years and ₹20,000 in 4 years at a simple interest rate.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Let P be the principal amount and r be the rate percentage per annum.

**Calculations:**

From the given data:

15000 = P + P × r × 2 / 100

20000 = P + P × r × 4 / 100

Let us denote the principal amount by P and the rate by r.

15000 = P (1 + 2r/100)

20000 = P (1 + 4r/100)

Dividing both equations:

⇒ 20000 / 15000 = (1 + 4r/100) / (1 + 2r/100)

⇒ 4 / 3 = (1 + 4r/100) / (1 + 2r/100)

Cross-multiplying to solve for r:

⇒ 4 (1 + 2r/100) = 3 (1 + 4r/100)

⇒ 4 + 8r/100 = 3 + 12r/100

⇒ 4 - 3 = 12r/100 - 8r/100

⇒ 1 = 4r/100

⇒ r = 100/4

⇒ r = 0.25 or 25%

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

⇒ (y - 2) × 5/18 × 9

⇒ (22 - 2) × 5/18 × 9

⇒ 20 × 5/2 = 50 m

**∴ The correct answer is 50 m.**

And speed of Madhur = 4km/h = 10/9 m/s

When two objects are running in the same direction

Then, relative speed = Difference of speed

For Raj, a - (5)/(9) = (x)/(9)

⇒ a = (5)/(9) + (x)/(9) ---------(1)

For Madhur, a - (10)/(9) = (x)/(10)

questions.question: A conical tent is to accommodate 12 persons. Each person must have 5 m² of the space on the ground and 20 m³ of air to breathe. The height of the tent should be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Height (h)** of a cone can be directly calculated from the ratio of **Volume (V)** and **Base Area (A)**.

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × Base Area × Height

Height (h) = (3 × Total Volume) ÷ Total Base Area

Since both depend on the **number of persons**, the height is: h = (3 × Air per person) ÷ Ground space per person

h = (3 × 20) ÷ 5 = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total persons = **12**

Ground space required per person = **5 m²**

Air required for breathing per person = **20 m³**

**Formula Used:**

Total Base Area = Number of persons × Area per person

Total Volume = Number of persons × Volume per person

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × πr²h (where πr² is the base area)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5a565d2f3ff71ba6f72c5bfdc19498a302824e1ed0f4bc507559ab2caa131a6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Base Area (πr²) = 12 × 5 = **60 m²**

⇒ Total Volume (V) = 12 × 20 = **240 m³**

⇒ Volume (V) = (1/3) × Base Area × Height (h)

⇒ 240 = (1/3) × 60 × h

⇒ 240 = 20 × h

⇒ h = 240 ÷ 20

⇒ h = **12 m**

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is exactly **one-third** the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Slant Height of a Cone

The relationship between height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) is given by the Pythagorean theorem: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the **lateral surface** of a cone is given by the formula: CSA = πrl.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total area includes the base and the curved surface: TSA = πr(l + r).</p

• This law was an early attempt to find patterns in the properties of elements.
 
• The law was based on the atomic weights of the elements known at that time.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right guarantees protection of interests of the minorities in the matter of their language, script or culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cultural and Educational Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Cultural and Educational Rights:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, specifically Articles 29 and 30 of the Indian Constitution, guarantees the protection of the interests of minorities.
 
• Article 29 ensures that any section of citizens residing in India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script, or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Article 30 grants all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• This right is designed to safeguard the diverse cultural fabric of India and prevent any form of cultural assimilation. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• These rights enable minorities to preserve their unique identities and promote their educational and cultural development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Right to Equality:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution, ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and abolishes untouchability.
 
• While essential for a just society, it does not specifically address the protection of minority languages, scripts, or cultures.
 
• This right focuses on equal treatment under the law, not specific cultural preservation.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Right to Freedom:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution, guarantees various freedoms, including freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• It also protects against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• While these freedoms are vital for individual liberty, they do not directly provide for the protection of minority cultural and educational interests.
 
• This right focuses on individual liberties regarding actions and expression.
 
• While freedom of expression can be used to promote minority cultures, the right to freedom does not directly protect the culture itself.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Right against Exploitation:**

 
 
• This fundamental right, outlined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution, prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and employment of children below the age of 14 in hazardous occupations.
 
• It aims to protect vulnerable sections of society from exploitation and abuse.
 
• While crucial for social justice, it does not pertain to the protection of minority languages, scripts, or cultures.
 
• This right is focused on preventing specific forms of human abuse and forced labour.
 
• This right is not related to cultural preservation.

questions.question: If the tax rate increases with the taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**progressive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Progressive:**

 
 
• A progressive tax system is one in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases.
 
• This means that higher-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes compared to lower-income earners.
 
• The intent of a progressive tax system is to distribute the tax burden more equitably, with those who have a greater ability to pay contributing a larger share.
 
• Income tax systems in many countries, including India and the United States, often use a progressive structure.
 
• Progressive taxation is often seen as a tool for reducing income inequality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regressive:**

 
 
• A regressive tax system is one in which the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases.
 
• This means that lower-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes compared to higher-income earners.
 
• Sales taxes and certain excise taxes can be considered regressive, as they take a larger proportion of income from those with lower incomes.
 
• Regressive taxes tend to exacerbate income inequality.
 
• These taxes place a higher burden on those who can least afford it.
 
 
 
• **Proportional:**
 
 
• A proportional tax system, also known as a flat tax, is one in which the tax rate remains constant regardless of the taxable amount.
 
• This means that everyone pays the same percentage of their income in taxes, regardless of their income level.
 
• While simple to administer, proportional taxes do not address income inequality.
 
• Everyone pays the same percentage of their income.
 
• This system is seen as being fair in that everyone is taxed at the same rate.
 
 
 
• **Digressive:**
 
 
• A digressive tax system is a tax system where the tax rate increases up to a certain point and then remains constant or decreases.
 
• It shares aspects of both progressive and proportional tax systems.
 
• It is less common than the other types of tax systems.
 
• The tax burden increases with income up to a specific income amount.
 
• After that amount the tax rate does not increase, or may decrease.
